Thailand Imposes Tariffs on Imported Satellite Dishes, Industry Faces Rising Costs

Thailand’s government has introduced a 25% tariff on imported satellite dishes and related receiving equipment, a move that has sent ripples through the country’s Cable & Satellite industry. The policy, which took effect last month, is part of a broader effort to promote domestic manufacturing capabilities within the sector.

Major industry players, including Eastern Signal Co. and ThaiSat Solutions, have reported immediate cost increases and disruptions in their supply chains. "We rely on imported components for over 60% of our satellite dish inventory," said Somchai Prasert, chief executive of Eastern Signal Co. "The new tariffs have raised our costs significantly, forcing us to review our pricing and production planning."

Smaller firms have been especially hard hit. At SkyView Broadcasting, a mid-sized operator based in Chonburi, management confirmed that the company had suspended new installations at several customer sites due to a shortage of satellite receivers. "We’ve had to halt work at four projects this week alone," said Surin Wongsuwan, operations manager. "As a result, we’ve reduced working hours for about 40 technicians."

Industry analysts say the measure is already affecting employment and investment decisions. According to a recent survey by the Thai Cable & Satellite Association, 72% of member companies reported delays in project timelines, and 39% anticipate temporary layoffs if the tariffs remain in place. "While the government’s intention is to strengthen local production, the immediate effect has been supply bottlenecks and pressure on margins," said analyst Nattapong Kittisak.

Officials at the Ministry of Commerce stated that the tariff would be reviewed in six months. In the meantime, industry representatives are calling for exemptions for certain high-tech components that are not produced locally, warning that prolonged restrictions could hamper the sector’s growth.
